reason: Live GET probes against Microsoft Graph with a delegated token decrypted from user_profiles. Raw payloads are in .probe-cache/ (gitignored).

items.question: $search on /events
items.conclusion: Do not use. List events documents OData query parameters and explicitly forbids $filter on recurrence; $search is not documented on either /events or calendarView. Search, attendee and category matching stay in-process over calendarView.

items.question: $orderby=start/dateTime on calendarView
items.conclusion: Could not reach calendarView: GET /me/calendars and GET /users/{email}/calendars both returned 403 ErrorAccessDenied (token has no Calendars.ReadWrite.Shared grant). Still sort in-process by start.dateTime. $top is documented: min 1, max 1000.

items.question: isDefaultCalendar on calendar resource
items.conclusion: Could not list calendars live: 403 ErrorAccessDenied. Until a token with Calendars.ReadWrite.Shared is probed, pair isDefaultCalendar with isTallyingResponses; do not treat isDefaultCalendar alone as proof a shared calendar is the owner's primary. list_calendars uses GET /users/{email}/calendars (equivalent to /me/calendars for the signed-in user).

items.question: GET /me/calendars vs GET /users/{email}/calendars
items.conclusion: Both paths returned 403 ErrorAccessDenied with this mail-only token, so equivalence is still unconfirmed live. GET /me succeeded, so the token is valid; calendar scopes are missing. list_calendars still uses /users/{email}/calendars for the signed-in user.

items.question: Does mailbox FullAccess appear in GET /users/{email}/calendars without an accepted calendar share?
items.conclusion: Could not list calendars live (403). Microsoft docs for GET /me/calendars (and the equivalent GET /users/{id}/calendars for the signed-in user) describe local copies from accepted calendar-sharing invitations, not Exchange mailbox FullAccess. Until probed with a calendar-scoped token, list_calendars unions GET /users/{caller}/calendars with GET /users/{owner}/calendars for each FullAccess owner. Folder-level mail shares are not used.

items.question: getSchedule address cap
items.conclusion: Maximum 20 entities per getSchedule call (users, DLs, or resources). Time window must be less than 62 days. Error 5006 when a slot contains more than 1000 entries.
